title: Split-emission machine
statement: For each nonnegative integer $k$, define a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k+1$ work tapes and state set $\{0,1,2,3\}$, initially in state $0$. In state $0$, if the first work-tape cell is blank, it stays in place, emits $0$, and enters state $2$; otherwise it stays in place, emits the scanned input bit if present, and enters state $1$. In state $1$ it moves the input head right, moves the first work head right, leaves the other work heads still, emits the scanned input bit if present, and returns to state $0$. In state $2$ it stays in place, emits $1$, and enters state $3$. In state $3$, if the scanned input cell contains a bit, it moves the input head right, emits that bit, and remains in state $3$; if the cell is blank, it stays in place, emits nothing, and halts. All work tapes are otherwise unchanged.
